title: logger-for-bash
intention: A FLIGHT RECORDER FOR BASH: source it, and what a script tried, what came back, and what it returned becomes a durable record instead of scrollback. One append-only file per namespace, capped at the last N lines, every line stamped <yyyymmdd.hhmmss.uuuuuu>.<pid> so concurrent shells stay separable. A child process renames the namespace for its own lifetime and leaves the parent's untouched — which is just how export works, so it costs nothing. Its first tenant is the boot: superclaude and launchers/bootstrap.sh route their steps through it, which is what makes the launcher's WATCHME emittable at all.
why: Akien, 2026-07-30, on the superclaude preflight: 'this is booting, it's a little weird, but it should log what the script tried, what worked, what didn't... i can think of 10M times that woulda been handy, just to have that running in the background.' Booting is precisely the moment when nothing else is up yet to observe you, so the launcher has to observe itself. And Law 3: a boot that leaves no record leaves every later question about it — did the repair run? did it work? was it slow? — to be re-derived by guessing, which is the defect Law 1 names.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured) — a boot that leaves no record cannot be reasoned about, only guessed at

Law 7 (loud at diagnostic surfaces, permanent in records of truth) — this is a DIAGNOSTIC surface, and the charter says so where it matters: the trim's small race is acceptable HERE and would not be in a record of truth
Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel) — the answer to 'what happened last boot' becomes a file instead of a re-derivation
the rescue ethos (launchers/intention+why.json) — it must never be able to break the shell that sourced it

proves_green.BUILDME: sourceable from ~/.bashrc and from superclaude without printing anything, without truncating, and without leaking a `set` into the caller
proves_green.PROVEME: bin/proofs/test_logger_for_bash.py (18 cases) green, including a non-vacuity case that runs the ORIGINAL and asserts it still FAILS the same fixtures

falsifier.proves_red: The recorded exit code can differ from the command's actual exit code; OR stderr can reach the terminal and miss the file; OR sourcing can truncate the record, print to stdout, or leak `set -e`/`set -u` into the caller; OR a trim can keep the OLDEST N; OR a record can land without its stamp+pid (which makes concurrent shells inseparable and the line cap meaningless).
falsifier.horizon: The four defects it was grafted to fix are measured PRESENT IN THE ORIGINAL by test_the_original_defects_are_real, which skips honestly (INDETERMINATE, never a quiet green) on a box where ~/dev/src/akientools is absent. If that graft source is ever fixed upstream, that case reds and says so — it is pinned to a file this repo does not own.
